judgments.yea_description: Voted for Legislative Bill 319, which would have restored food assistance to most people with drug felony convictions. Federal law bars anyone convicted of a drug felony from food assistance for life, and lets a state opt out. Nebraska has opted out only part way. Today a person with one or two convictions for possessing or using drugs can get help if they are in, or have finished, a treatment program. A person with three or more, or with any conviction for selling drugs, gets nothing. The bill would have opened the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program to anyone with a drug felony once they had finished their sentence. They would also have been eligible while on parole, probation or post-release supervision. One condition would have stayed. A person with three or more convictions for possessing or using drugs would still have needed to be in, or have finished, a licensed treatment program. A licensed health care provider could have waived that by finding the person did not need treatment. The Nebraska Legislature passed it 32-17, the Governor vetoed it, and the vote to override the veto failed 24 to 24, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Legislative Bill 929, which would have let Medicaid managed care companies pay a patient's copay for them. Nebraska's Medicaid program may charge patients premiums, copays and deductibles. The bill would not have changed that power. It would have required the state to let a managed care company pay a patient's deductible, copay, coinsurance or similar charge on the patient's behalf, where federal law allows it. An earlier draft would have banned most of those charges outright and delayed the rest to October 2028. That part was removed before the final vote. The Nebraska Legislature passed it 31-18, the Governor vetoed it, and the vote to override the veto failed 22 to 26, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Legislative Bill 1029, which would have narrowed what public colleges must report about money from hostile foreign governments. Nebraska law makes a public college report funding and contracts it gets from a foreign adversarial source. The bill would have counted a contract only where it benefits that foreign source. It would also have taken salary, wages and other pay out of what has to be reported at all. Less of the money coming from those sources would have been disclosed. The Nebraska Legislature passed it 29-20, the Governor vetoed it, the Legislature did not vote to override, and it did not become law.
